guard: a creds-source endpoint never presents its cached credential after that credential has expired
why: The endpoint's pre-connect refresh is deliberately best-effort after the first connection. If
the source is down when the cached cred expires, removing this guard lets connectAndBind
present credential material it has already decoded as expired. The live smoke captures the
disposable broker's authentication-expired denial so a presentation is a real dial, not a
local parser check.
75%/100% gap (H2): credsRenewalDelayMs fires a stale rebuild at 75% of iat→exp; the guard
refuses at 100%. At expiresInSeconds:3 that interval is 750ms (2.25s to 3.0s), two source
constants, not a machine race. A mutated connectAndBind in that window still dials a valid
cached cred.
Source recovery used to be a read count. That count has no relationship to the clock the
guard reads (Date.now vs credsClaims.exp), so a source that returned on the second fail
could mint while the original connection was still live. Time-based recovery after exp
fixed that mismatch. A clock offset after exp still does not outlast the broker's close.
A presentation is cid-correlated: the window cid logs User JWT no longer valid and
Authentication Failure, has a non-empty history, and never logged Authenticated JWT.
Live-connection expiry (User Authentication Expired after a successful auth) is not a
presentation (#1408). Non-vacuity is client-side: a post-exp source read plus the pre-dial
refusal warning. The broker window is the violation detector only.
Drain race: the 1s bounded wait returns on the first byte past the marker (often a cid
create). Capture can lag a real dial, so an empty slice is not a hard fail. CLASSIFY
re-slices after +4s; the named cell still uses slice1.
#1411 two-producer: nats.js internal reconnects present currentCreds through the getter
with no expiry check. An unmutated run with the guard present has emitted JWT-expired +
Authentication Failure on that path (reviewer run 4, inWindow=false). A denial in the log
is therefore not mutation-owned by window position. H1 (75% stale rebuild the broker later
expires live) stays out of the window; widening to catch it would re-admit live-expiry.
Hold cap is inert in the interval it was meant to bound. After the 75% fail the next
source timer is CREDS_RETRY_MS=60s, so no source read occurs between exp+1500ms and the
broker close. 'cap reached 0/5' is not evidence the ceiling was comfortable.
Mutated named-cell discrimination, pooled across every 5-run whose split is still named
after the cid-correlated detector (n=20): 12 RED / 8 SURVIVED. That is not a measured
60% property of the fixture (the 95% interval on 12/20 is roughly 0.36 to 0.81); it
establishes that the cell is not deterministic. Batches: post-detector soundness 3/5,
exp+1500 3/5, exp+1500 with CLASSIFY extra drain 4/5, event-anchor 2/5. A fifth 5-run
(source held past exp, no +1500) completed and was not 5/5; its per-run logs are gone
and the final split is not restated here. Per-batch 3/5 vs 4/5 vs 2/5 are not
distinguishable from sampling noise at n=5. The cell is blocked on #1411 deciding
whether the getter reconnect is in scope. Do not mint already-expired material. Do not
widen the window. expectRed is the original name.

mutations.name: the creds pre-dial expiry guard is removed
mutations.expectRed: a rebuild presents cached expired creds to the broker ZERO times after renewal fails
mutations.cell: a rebuild presents cached expired creds to the broker ZERO times after renewal fails
mutations.note: Deleting the block is the issue's pre-fix behavior and leaves the tree compiling. The source fails twice, so the first reconnect dials the cached expired cred and the broker logs the denial before the source recovers.
